drhp.business: We provide a range of technology-enabled diagnostic services such as radiology, clinical laboratory and nuclear medicine service to public hospitals, private hospitals, certain PSU (Public Sector Undertaking) of Government of India and medical colleges across tier I, tier II and tier III cities throughout India. We provide healthcare services for core testing, patients diagnosis, disease prevention and monitoring of various health conditions. We offer a one-stop solution for all services to our patients through our operational network.
drhp.one_liner: We provide a range of technology-enabled diagnostic services such as radiology, clinical laboratory and nuclear medicine service to public hospitals, private hospitals, certain PSU (Public Sector Undertaking) of Government of India and medical colleges across tier I, tier II and tier III cities …
risks: This heavy reliance on radiology services implies that any disruptions, challenges, or shifts in market dynamics specific to this domain could have a disproportionate impact on our overall business.
Any inability to effectively assess demand, establish reliable supplier networks, or manage operations in such new locations may result in lower-than-expected returns or operational inefficiencies.

In the event of a regional slowdown in the economic activity in these regions, or any other developments including political or civil unrest, disruption or sustained economic downturn that reduce the demand for our services in these regions, could adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations, which are largely dependent on the performance and other prevailing conditions affecting the economies of these regions.
We are majorly dependent on certain key customers cum patients for a substantial portion of our revenues.
Loss of relationship with any of these customers cum patients may have a material adverse effect on our profitability and results of operations.
A portion of our revenue from operations is derived from a limited number of key customers cum patients.

Finding new customers cum patients with comparable advertising expenditure might prove challenging, time-consuming and potentially more expensive due to increased customers cum patients acquisition costs.
Furthermore, the loss of any of these key customers cum patients could potentially have a detrimental effect on our market standing and reputation.

business_ops.supply_chain_integration: Diagnostic centres largely operate within partner hospital/PSU premises under MOUs (asset-light real-estate model), with the Company procuring, installing and maintaining its own diagnostic equipment (MRI, CT, X-ray, ultrasound, mammography, DEXA, PET-CT, etc.) and maintaining vendor relationships for procurement, pricing and fleet-wide maintenance. The Vijayawada processing unit-cum-laboratory and 24x7 teleradiology hub centralise sample processing and image reporting for centres across the network; in one West Bengal PSU arrangement the imaging equipment is instead provided by the PSU and diagnostic reporting is undertaken by them, with the Company's scope limited to operation and maintenance.

genesis.founding_story: Initial subscribers to the Memorandum of Association were Mr. Raja Rao Yalamanchili and Ms. Hymavathi Yalamanchali. In 2015, Dr. Kuldeep Kumar Chalasani and Dr. Chalasani Kavitha were appointed Directors on the Board. In 2016 the original shareholders transferred certain equity shares to Sri Ram Medicare Private Limited and Infer Radiological and Imaging Services Pvt Ltd (entities in which Dr. Chalasani Kuldeep Kumar and Dr. Chalasani Kavitha were MOA subscribers), and in 2018 the original shareholders transferred their entire remaining shareholding to Dr. Chalasani Kuldeep Kumar and Dr. Chalasani Kavitha, who assumed control and management of the Company.

internal_operational.risk: This heavy reliance on radiology services implies that any disruptions, challenges, or shifts in market dynamics specific to this domain could have a disproportionate impact on our overall business.

In the event of a regional slowdown in the economic activity in these regions, or any other developments including political or civil unrest, disruption or sustained economic downturn that reduce the demand for our services in these regions, could adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations, which are largely dependent on the performance and other prevailing conditions affecting the economies of these regions.

strategy_growth.risk: We have information technology systems that support our business processes, including for conducting tests, transmission of test results, billing services, quality control, human resources, finance and other patient service functions.

If we experience system interruptions, errors or downtime (which could result from various causes, including changes in client use patterns, technological failure, changes to systems, linkages with third-party systems and power failures) or if we are unable to access necessary technology to effectively serve our patients and manage our operations, our business prospects and financial performance could be materially and adversely affected.

concerns_observed: Despite the declining trend, customer concentration remains high: top-1 customer contributed 44.17% and top-5 customers 64.32% of FY26 revenue.

54.19% of FY26 revenue (down from 77.22% FY24) comes from Public-Private-Partnership MOUs with government counterparties at MOU-fixed prices, and 61.46% of FY26 revenue (Rs.3,828.07 lakhs) is B2G; trade receivables were Rs.1,740.05 lakhs at FY26-end.

Related-party transactions were Rs.1,031.89 lakhs (16.57% of revenue) in FY26 and Rs.1,908.28 lakhs (49.91% of revenue) in FY25, including a Rs.495.00 lakhs corporate guarantee to HDFC Bank on behalf of promoter-group entity Sri Ram Medicare Private Limited, outstanding in all three years.

A 12:1 bonus issue of 1,54,10,580 equity shares was allotted March 21, 2026 (nil consideration), less than five months before this RHP; weighted average secondary-transaction cost of acquisition is Rs.34.95 per share against an Offer Price not yet disclosed.

Total debt rose to Rs.1,784.82 lakhs at FY26-end (from Rs.1,081.42 lakhs FY25) across 17 separate loan facilities from Axis Bank, Indusind Bank, Kotak Mahindra Bank, HDFC Bank, Moneywise Financial Services and Bajaj Finance, with rates up to 12.0% (Moneywise term loan, Rs.661.21 lakhs) and an HDFC Bank car loan of Rs.80.00 lakhs flagged as non-business-purpose.

62.63% of the Rs.4,514.85 lakhs equipment capex funded from Net Proceeds has no purchase order placed yet (Manjeri MRI Rs.875 lakhs, Vijayawada CT Rs.700 lakhs, both Bangalore items Rs.1,125 lakhs, etc.), and a further tranche is earmarked for unidentified, unappraised inorganic acquisitions capped at 25% of Gross Proceeds.

Group companies in the same line of business posted losses: Vista Pramodini Medicare Private Limited (Rs.318.88 lakhs loss FY26, Rs.277.99 lakhs FY25, Rs.328.81 lakhs FY24), with no non-compete agreement against Infer Radiological and Imaging Services Private Limited or Vista Pramodini Medicare.
Promoters and Promoter Group are expected to retain 62.64% of post-Offer equity, continuing majority control over Board, capex and dividend decisions.

verdict.our_read: Pramodini Medicare is an Andhra Pradesh-rooted, MOU/PPP-based radiology-led diagnostics operator (16 centres, 7 states, FY26 EBITDA margin 49.61%, RONW 32.69%) whose de-risking story (AP revenue share down from 86.66% FY24 to 61.90% FY26, top-1 customer down from 63.88% to 44.17%) is still incomplete, with 54.19% of FY26 revenue tied to government PPP MOUs and 62.63% of the IPO-funded equipment capex not yet ordered.
post_listing_commitments: Entire Net Proceeds of the Fresh Offer are proposed to be deployed by Fiscal 2026-27, with any balance utilised in Fiscal 2027-28, primarily Rs.4,514.85 lakhs toward medical-equipment capex for existing (Hubli, Manjeri, Vijayawada) and proposed (Bangalore) diagnostic centres.

Remaining Net Proceeds are earmarked for unidentified inorganic acquisitions and general corporate purposes, capped at 35% of Gross Proceeds combined (GCP capped at the lower of 15% of Gross Proceeds or Rs.10 crore; acquisitions capped at 25%).
red_flags: Promoter-Directors Dr. Chalasani Kuldeep Kumar and Dr. Chalasani Kavitha were disqualified under Section 164(2) of the Companies Act, 2013 from November 1, 2015 to October 31, 2021 (removed January 10, 2018) due to non-filing by another company, M/s. Lark Avenues Private Limited.

Charge was not created within the applicable timeline for an Axis Bank Ltd medical-equipment loan (sanction letter dated May 28, 2025); the Company has filed Form CHG-1 and a compounding application (e-Form GNL-1, SRN AC3070601, dated April 18, 2026) for the resulting Companies Act non-compliance.
Independent Director Dr. Eshwar Chandra Nandury has formally declined, in writing, to furnish his bank statements and income tax returns to the Company.
strengths_observed: Revenue grew 63.0% YoY to Rs.6,228.75 lakhs in FY26 (from Rs.3,823.77 lakhs FY25 and Rs.3,522.95 lakhs FY24), with PAT rising from Rs.693.01 lakhs (FY24) to Rs.1,737.73 lakhs (FY26), a 2.5x increase over two years.
EBITDA margin of 49.61% and PAT margin of 27.9% in FY26, alongside ROE 39.08%, ROCE 34.66% and RONW 32.69% for FY26.

Geographic diversification is underway: Andhra Pradesh's share of revenue fell from 86.66% (FY24) to 61.90% (FY26) as Karnataka (20.82% FY26, from 0% FY24) and West Bengal (7.27% FY26, from 0%) contributed for the first time.
Customer concentration has been declining: top-1 customer share fell from 63.88% (FY24) to 44.17% (FY26) and top-5 from 80.87% to 64.32% over the same period.
None of the Promoters'/Promoter Group's 85.71% pre-Offer shareholding (1,43,09,477 shares) is pledged or encumbered.

Asset-light hospital/PSU-partnership model: 16 diagnostic centres across 7 states operate largely within partner-hospital premises under MOUs, with the Company owning and maintaining the diagnostic equipment (7 MRI, 8 CT, 1 PET-CT, 20 X-ray, 15 ultrasound systems as of March 31, 2026).

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Diagnostic centres largely operate within partner hospital/PSU premises under MOUs (asset-light real-estate model), with the Company procuring, installing and maintaining its own diagnostic equipment (MRI, CT, X-ray, ultrasound, mammography, DEXA, PET-CT, etc.) and maintaining vendor relationships for procurement, pricing and fleet-wide maintenance. The Vijayawada processing unit-cum-laboratory and 24x7 teleradiology hub centralise sample processing and image reporting for centres across the network; in one West Bengal PSU arrangement the imaging equipment is instead provided by the PSU and diagnostic reporting is undertaken by them, with the Company's scope limited to operation and maintenance.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- This heavy reliance on radiology services implies that any disruptions, challenges, or shifts in market dynamics specific to this domain could have a disproportionate impact on our overall business.
- Any inability to effectively assess demand, establish reliable supplier networks, or manage operations in such new locations may result in lower-than-expected returns or operational inefficiencies.
- In the event of a regional slowdown in the economic activity in these regions, or any other developments including political or civil unrest, disruption or sustained economic downturn that reduce the demand for our services in these regions, could adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations, which are largely dependent on the performance and other prevailing conditions affecting the economies of these regions.
- We are majorly dependent on certain key customers cum patients for a substantial portion of our revenues.
- Loss of relationship with any of these customers cum patients may have a material adverse effect on our profitability and results of operations.
- A portion of our revenue from operations is derived from a limited number of key customers cum patients.
- Finding new customers cum patients with comparable advertising expenditure might prove challenging, time-consuming and potentially more expensive due to increased customers cum patients acquisition costs.
- Furthermore, the loss of any of these key customers cum patients could potentially have a detrimental effect on our market standing and reputation.
